Done. Written to `operations/engineering/fars/docs/tech-spec-mapping.md`.

**What I found**: 110+ spec files covering every layer of the system from mathematical foundations (σ/Δ nuclei, fiber Heyting algebras) through architecture (relational machine, four-component automaton) to institutional theory (captain as nuclear witness, fiduciary coalgebra).

**Current system state**: FARS layer (flatfile, hooks, MCP) is solid. ARS layer (agents, skills, commands) is strong. The knowledge graph and operational records work. The primary gap is the formal mathematical layer — σ/Δ nuclei, closure operators, Heyting semantics exist only in specs.

**Top 3 highest-leverage implementations**:
1. **CDS** (cellular-data-serialization) — the data format everything builds on
2. **RES** (relation-expression-syntax) — small language for fiber propositions, implementable quickly
3. **CCE** (cellular-closure-engine) — the computation kernel with deterministic σ/Δ stabilization

The cellular closure computing specs are by far the most implementation-ready — they include error codes, memory layouts, RPC protocols, and deterministic algorithms. They're the bridge between our working system and its mathematical description.
